title: Champions, Calm Waters, and Steady Numbers
overview: A celebratory Monday: Türkiye's women's volleyball team, the "Sultans of the Net," defended their European title with a five-set win over Italy, dominating headlines across nearly every outlet. Meanwhile, regional tensions around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's announced "exclusion zone" bear watching for anyone with travel or shipping ties to the Gulf, though there's no direct impact on daily life in Türkiye yet. On the practical side, inflation continues to cool, ikamet numbers were published for at least one province, and the US has confirmed a resumption of visa services in Turkey.

sections.heading: Sultans of the Net Take Europe Again
sections.body: Türkiye's women's volleyball team beat Italy 3-2 in a five-set thriller to retain their European championship, a result covered warmly across the spectrum — from state media (Anadolu Ajansı) to pro-government outlets (Milliyet, Hürriyet, Türkiye Today) to opposition-leaning Cumhuriyet and independent Bianet. It's a rare story with no divergence in framing: everyone's celebrating together, which says something pleasant about shared national moments cutting across otherwise polarized media.

sections.heading: Visas and Residency: Practical Notes
sections.body: The US has confirmed visa services will resume in Turkey following an earlier dispute, welcome news for anyone with pending applications or family visits planned. Separately, Gümüşhane province released updated figures on foreign residence permit holders, part of routine regional reporting; residents elsewhere should expect similar local disclosures. Fragomen also flagged new minimum salary changes, which can affect work-permit thresholds — worth checking if your permit or employer sponsorship depends on salary minimums.

sections.heading: Gulf Tensions: Watch, Don't Worry Yet
sections.body: Iran says it will announce a new 'exclusion zone' near the Strait of Hormuz, and separately claims a strike on a US ship there, which Washington denies. There's no confirmed escalation affecting Turkish waters or air corridors, and Türkiye's own US travel advisory remains unchanged at Level 2. Still, anyone with travel plans through the Gulf region (Iran, Iraq, Syria, Lebanon remain Level 4) should monitor official advisories rather than headlines alone.

sections.heading: Money: Inflation Eases, Growth Outlook Trimmed
sections.body: August inflation cooled to 31.5%, continuing a gradual downward trend, though analysts at AGBI note it's still too high for an interest rate cut soon. The central bank added 16 tons of gold to reserves, a modest confidence signal. Separately, Turkey's 2027 growth outlook was revised down slightly as authorities balance price stability against expansion — nothing dramatic, but a reminder that budgeting for the year ahead should stay conservative. Exchange rates held steady: USD/TRY 48.42, EUR/TRY 56.24, GBP/TRY 65.47.

sections.heading: Faith and Community Notes
sections.body: Quietly, this week's rights coverage was gentle: the Armenian Patriarch prayed for restored Turkish-Armenian ties, and worshippers gathered for the annual service at Akdamar Island's historic church — both covered plainly by pro-government outlets. No major court rulings or residency-related legal actions were reported today affecting foreign residents specifically.

closing: Enjoy the volleyball glow — and maybe a çay to celebrate.
